title: Common Ports for Azure Administrators
summary: Ports and special addresses that appear in NSG, firewall and connectivity questions.

sections.heading: Management & web
rows: HTTPS; Azure Bastion sessions; SSTP and OpenVPN P2S; Azure File Sync agent

sections.heading: Data & file services
rows: SMB — mounting Azure Files (often blocked by ISPs)

sections.heading: Special addresses
items: 168.63.129.16 — Azure platform virtual IP: Azure-provided DNS, Load Balancer health probes (AzureLoadBalancer tag), VM agent communication. Don't block it.
169.254.169.254 — Azure Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) and managed identity token endpoint, reachable only from inside a VM.
Azure reserves the first four and the last IP address of every subnet.

title: RBAC Scopes & Inheritance
summary: Where role assignments can be made and how they combine.

sections.heading: Scopes (broadest to narrowest)
rows: All child MGs, subscriptions, RGs, resources
All RGs and resources in the subscription

sections.heading: Rules to remember
items: Assignments inherit downward; you can't block inheritance (only deny assignments subtract).
Effective access = union of all roles from all group memberships and parent scopes.
Assign to groups, at the narrowest scope, with the least-privileged role.
NotActions subtracts from one role's Actions; it is not a deny.
Changes can take a few minutes to apply; sign out/in to refresh tokens.

title: Storage Redundancy at a Glance
summary: Copies, placement and what each option survives.

sections.heading: Gotchas
items: Premium accounts: LRS or ZRS only.
Geo-replication is asynchronous — check Last Sync Time for potential data loss.
Secondary endpoint: <account>-secondary.blob.core.windows.net (RA options).
Redundancy isn't backup — deletions replicate too. Use soft delete, versioning or Azure Backup.

title: Blob Access Tiers
summary: Hot, Cool, Cold and Archive compared.

sections.heading: Tiers
rows: Rare access, must stay immediately readable

sections.heading: Remember
items: Cooler tiers: cheaper storage, more expensive access.
Early deletion/tier-change before the minimum is charged pro-rata.
Archive rehydration: standard priority can take up to ~15 hours; high priority is faster for smaller objects.
Set tiers per blob or automate with lifecycle management rules.
Archive is supported on LRS, GRS and RA-GRS accounts.

versionNote: Retention minimums, rehydration times and redundancy support may change; verify on Microsoft Learn.

title: VNet & Subnet Rules
summary: Address planning, reserved addresses and special subnets.

sections.heading: Rules
items: A VNet lives in one region and one subscription.
Address spaces must not overlap with peered or connected networks.
Subnets in a VNet communicate by default.
Peering is non-transitive; gateway transit shares a hub gateway.
Route tables and NSGs attach to subnets (NSGs also to NICs).

title: NSG Behavior
summary: Priorities, defaults and evaluation order in one place.

sections.heading: Evaluation
items: Custom priorities 100–4096; lowest number first; first match wins.
Inbound: subnet NSG → NIC NSG. Outbound: NIC NSG → subnet NSG. Both must allow.
Stateful — return traffic is allowed automatically.
ASGs must be in the same VNet as the NICs they group.
Tools: Effective security rules, IP flow verify, NSG diagnostics.

title: Choosing a Load-Balancing Service
summary: Load Balancer, Application Gateway, Front Door and Traffic Manager on one page.

sections.heading: Decision table
rows: Non-HTTP traffic, internal tiers, highest performance
Path/host routing, TLS offload, WAF in one region
Global web apps, edge acceleration, global WAF
Global routing for any protocol (priority, weighted, performance, geographic)

sections.heading: Quick cues
items: 'URL path' or 'WAF' + one region → Application Gateway.
'Any TCP port' or 'internal' → Load Balancer.
'Users worldwide' + HTTP → Front Door.
'DNS-based failover between regions' → Traffic Manager.

title: Azure DNS Concepts
summary: Record types, zones and resolution rules.

sections.heading: Record types
rows: Alias to another name (not allowed at the zone apex)
Text, e.g., domain verification (App Service asuid)
Name servers that are authoritative for the zone
Points to an Azure resource; works at the apex

sections.heading: Public vs private
items: Public zone: delegate by setting the registrar's NS records to Azure's name servers.
Private zone: link to VNets; enable auto-registration on one zone per VNet.
Azure-provided DNS: 168.63.129.16.
Custom DNS servers must forward to 168.63.129.16 for private zones.
Hybrid: DNS Private Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints.

sections.heading: Terms
rows: Automatic numeric data from Azure resources (93 days)
Per-resource operation logs; need a diagnostic setting
Routes logs/metrics to Log Analytics, storage, Event Hubs or partners
Collects guest OS data per data collection rules
What to collect and where to send it
Condition on metrics, logs or activity log
Suppress or add actions to fired alerts (e.g., maintenance)
Curated monitoring for VMs, storage, networks, containers
Interactive report combining text, queries and charts

sections.heading: KQL starter
items: Heartbeat | summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer
AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue endswith "DELETE" | project TimeGenerated, Caller, ResourceId
Perf | where CounterName == "% Processor Time" | summarize avg(CounterValue) by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m), Computer
Event | where EventLevelName == "Error" | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) | count

title: VM Availability Options
summary: From single VMs to multi-region designs.

sections.heading: Options
rows: Lowest SLA; still a single point of failure
Up to 3 FDs, up to 20 UDs (default 5); one datacenter
Deploy 2+ VMs across zones; highest VM SLA
Hardware and zone failures; load changes

sections.heading: Rules
items: Choose availability options at creation time.
A VM can't be in both an availability set and a zone.
Use Standard LB and Standard public IPs for zone-redundant frontends.
Check the published SLA document for current percentages.
